verdict.why: The left build carries more of the brief's named features (a visible cupola with weather vane, hay bales, a fence, a stone base, and big white-trimmed doors), but its crenellated roof edges and checkerboard facade make it read partly as a fortress. The right build is cleaner and more coherent in massing and palette, with a stone plinth, timber framing, and a well-resolved gable, yet it has no cupola or vane and its hay bales are barely visible, so it reads more as a red timber house than a farm barn.
